agentCan: Build the connect flow against the authorize endpoint and the API
Design for the documented rate limits (especially deploy ceilings)

approval.trigger: None documented. The docs describe no review, approval, verification, or listing step before real users can connect an OAuth application, and no marketplace/listing program for OAuth apps at all. No user caps before approval are stated, because there is no approval concept in the docs. Treat 'no review' as 'no review documented', not a stated policy.

blockers.detail: docs.netlify.com describes no scope parameter or permission granularity for OAuth applications: nothing in the docs lets a developer request read-only or site-limited access. Authorization appears to be all-or-nothing at the account level (the docs simply don't specify). This is the biggest surprise for developers coming from GitHub/Google-style scoped OAuth.
blockers.howToClear: No documented clearance; design your product and your consent copy around account-level access.
blockers.title: No documented scopes

blockers.detail: The API get-started page never states access-token expiry, refresh tokens, or grant types for OAuth apps, and the canonical docs defer flow details to a blog post. (By contrast, PATs do get a documented, user-chosen expiration date at creation, a control the OAuth-app docs don't mention.)
blockers.howToClear: Verify behavior empirically in a test account before promising token behavior to users; keep the unverified list in this guide attached to your launch checklist.
blockers.title: No documented token lifecycle

tested: Read-only verification: registration location, credential issuance, the authorize endpoint, revocation path, and rate limits were checked against current docs.netlify.com pages (no application registered, nothing submitted). The thinness of the documentation is itself a verified finding here.
unverified: Grant types supported (authorization code, implicit/ticket, etc.), the token endpoint URL, and PKCE support.

Any review, verification, listing, or fees: none mentioned anywhere in the docs read.
What exactly a user sees on the authorize/consent screen.

alternatives: Personal Access Tokens (your own scripts/CLI use: 'Use your PAT for manual authentication in shell scripts'; not a multi-user product mechanism)
flavor.recommended: An OAuth application registered under User settings > Applications > OAuth applications, used with the OAuth2 authorize endpoint at app.netlify.com/authorize
flavor.why: 'When you register an application, Netlify will provide a client ID and secret you can use in your application settings.' The docs are explicit about when to use it: 'If you're making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2. This allows users to authorize your application to use Netlify on their behalf without having to copy/paste API tokens or touch sensitive login info.' There is effectively one flavor.

humanMust: Register the OAuth application in user settings and custody the client secret
Verify the undocumented parts (grant type, token endpoint, expiry) empirically before launch, because the docs do not state them
name: Netlify
nuances: Rate limits bite deploy-heavy agents: 500 requests per minute for most API requests, but API deploys are limited to 3 per minute and 100 per day (higher only by contacting Netlify). List responses paginate at 100 items per page.

Revocation is user-controlled and silent: users revoke under User settings > Applications > Authorized applications ('Options > Revoke access'); the docs describe no webhook or notification to the developer.
SAML wrinkle (PATs only): PAT creation has an 'Allow access to my SAML-based Netlify team' toggle; the OAuth-app docs mention no equivalent consideration.
prerequisites: A Netlify account (registration lives in your user settings)

steps.detail: In the Netlify UI: avatar > User settings > Applications > OAuth applications > register a new application. Netlify issues a client ID and client secret. (The docs confirm where registration lives and what you receive; they do not enumerate the form's fields.)
steps.title: Register an OAuth application

steps.detail: Direct users to app.netlify.com/authorize so they can authorize your application; then call the Netlify API (api.netlify.com/api/v1/...) with the resulting token as Authorization: Bearer. Note: the docs do not document the token endpoint, grant types, or redirect-URI registration on docs.netlify.com; the get-started page defers flow details to a Netlify blog post.
steps.title: Build the connect flow

steps.detail: Users who authorized your app see it under User settings > Applications > Authorized applications and can revoke it there. Expect silent revocations; poll for 401s and prompt reconnect.
steps.title: Handle revocation

tagline: The most minimal OAuth program in the library: register an application in your user settings, get a client ID and secret, send users to the authorize endpoint. The docs describe no scopes, no review, no marketplace, and no token expiry rules; the surprises are what is missing.

time.active: ~5 min registration + ~1 hr of flow code
time.total: Same day; nothing documented stands in front of users
